statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures remain halted since the Friday settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any hour of this horizon and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor, while Stress stays in the elevated band on a verified Saturday US-Iran tanker exchange that has since hardened in rhetoric.
recommendation: Tail holds a closed-venue floor of 4-5% across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress starts at 50% and drifts to 57%, inside the elevated band for the whole horizon, reflecting Saturday's verified US-Iran exchange and the subsequent US threat to sink Iranian tankers, a hawkish September rate path after the payroll beat, an impaired Strait of Hormuz, an unpriced Friday trade-embargo ultimatum tied to Fed policy, and a data-heavy week containing August PPI on 10 September and August CPI on 11 September. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt as the US-Iran tanker exchange hardens into an explicit threat to sink Iranian shipping, a Friday embargo ultimatum tied to Fed policy stays unpriced, and Labor Day pushes the first US cash session to 8 September
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions during that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. Since the previous assessment the verified Saturday sequence has hardened rather than resolved. NBC News, the Associated Press and The Jerusalem Post report that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer, that both vessels evaded and no US personnel were harmed, and that US forces disabled the tankers M/T Downy and M/T Stark 1 near Kharg Island and destroyed M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman after its crew was evacuated. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper framed the response in explicitly economic terms, and the US Defense Secretary subsequently stated publicly that continued Iranian fire at US ships would be answered by destroying and sinking Iranian oil tankers. Iranian state-linked media confirmed a strike near the Kharg anchorage with no casualties reported, and no Iranian counter-response has been verified at this assessment cutoff. A second unpriced thread is policy rather than military. On Friday the US President tied a threatened halt of trade with deficit partners to a demand that the Federal Reserve lower rates, after July trade data showed the deficit widening to $88.6 billion, and repeated the threat to reporters. That headline is two-sided and remains unresolved into the restart. All of it lands unpriced, because CME equity-index futures have been halted since the 21:00 UTC Friday settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly seven hours after the last hour published here, with Labor Day on Monday 7 September pushing the first US cash equity session of the week to Tuesday 8 September. The energy channel remains the transmission path to watch: WTI settled at $91.48 after a weekly advance near 10% and Brent at $96.28 after 7.6%, Strait of Hormuz commodity transits ran well below their recent average, and US retail diesel set a record $5.85 per gallon. Rates are the third input: August nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 with unemployment unchanged at 4.1% and 55,000 of upward revisions to prior months, lifting priced odds of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC toward 60%, while the latest Federal Reserve H.15 observation carries the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77%. The VIX settled at 14.53, far below any level associated with disorderly repricing. Friday's internals were split rather than aligned: semiconductors were broadly higher while five of eight megacaps fell, and the S&P 500 and Dow both closed lower even as the Nasdaq-100 finished higher. That is an internally mixed signature, not the aligned cross-asset stack a genuine tail regime requires. Because no forecast hour in this assessment can contain an observable price path, Tail is scored at a closed-venue floor throughout rather than from any directional view, and the whole of the accumulating weight is carried by Stress, which sits in the elevated band across the horizon. The first genuine price-path evaluation of the new week belongs to a later assessment run made after the Globex restart.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the closing five hours of the August payroll session and the first nineteen hours of the CME weekend halt. The 16:00 UTC hour on 4 September was already past the release peak at Tail 15% and Stress 53% under a mixed mode, and every slot in this window maps to EA_ON and green. Tail decayed steadily through the remainder of the US cash session as the index retraced its highs and recovered, reaching Tail 12% and Stress 48% by 20:00 UTC with semiconductor leadership diverging from a softer broad tape. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% with mode normal, while Stress eased to 38% and then drifted back up through the Saturday hours, reaching 48% at 15:00 UTC as the unpriced weekend stack accumulated. All 24 slots carry a published Claude assessment.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress opens at 50% and drifts to a 57% peak, inside the elevated band for the whole horizon, reflecting Saturday's verified US-Iran exchange and the subsequent explicit US threat to sink Iranian tankers, hawkish September rate pricing after the payroll beat, an energy premium from continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, an unresolved Friday trade-embargo ultimatum tied to Fed policy, and an open two-sided headline window that would express in a single reopening auction. Mode is characterised as normal through the dormant hours and mixed from 08:00 UTC on 6 September, where the accumulated stack is genuinely two-sided. Confidence eases from 86% to 79% purely through the ageing of Friday-anchored levels and Saturday reporting, staying inside the high band because coverage is complete and every material input was verified. The horizon ends at 15:00 UTC on 6 September, roughly seven hours before the scheduled 22:00 UTC Globex restart, so the reopening auction and any gap it produces belong to a later assessment run, with Labor Day on 7 September thinning the sessions that immediately follow.
